concept: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds

claims.text: Inspect pg_index.indisvalid for query eligibility and indisready for INSERT/UPDATE maintenance; indisready=false means writes ignore the index, so invalid does not imply one universal maintenance state. (low confidence)

Deadlocks or uniqueness errors during concurrent scanning can leave invalid indexes that queries cannot use; pganalyze independently documents failed or aborted concurrent builds as a typical cause. (high confidence)
A unique concurrent build starts enforcing uniqueness during its second scan; failure there can leave uniqueness enforcement active even though queries cannot use the index. (medium confidence)

Blind retries can fail with relation already exists; IF NOT EXISTS only checks name existence and cannot establish that the existing index is usable or matches the intended definition. (medium confidence)
A running concurrent build is initially invalid too; indisvalid=false alone cannot establish that creation has failed. (medium confidence)
Concurrent creation uses multiple transactions; cancellation after catalog creation can leave an INVALID index, unlike an aborted ordinary build. (medium confidence)
Invalid artifacts can occupy disk and incur write maintenance despite providing no query acceleration; dbi demonstrates a sequential scan and subsequent index growth. (high confidence)
Drop and recreate a failed index, or use REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY; the latter is the REINDEX form that can concurrently rebuild an invalid index. (medium confidence)

After failed concurrent reindexing, an INVALID _ccnew artifact represents the unfinished replacement; drop it and retry. An INVALID _ccold artifact is the old index left after successful rebuilding; drop it. Numeric suffixes may follow these names. (low confidence)
